focus: Job Setup → Automations — apply response template subject

environment_issue.summary: Server is running from branch 'feature-ai-credits-summaries-scoring-qa', NOT 'messaging-improvements' where the email-subjects feature was implemented. The feature code (commit e7f272279) exists only on 'messaging-improvements' and 'messaging-improvements-qa' branches. All test scenarios are untestable because the feature is not deployed to the running server.
environment_issue.details: The running server at http://app.lvh.me:5007 serves code from a branch that does not contain any email-subjects changes. The JobSetupAutomations component on the current branch has no applyResponseTemplateSubject state, no FormInput for subject, and the jobs table schema has no apply_response_template_subject column.

scenarios.description: Navigate to a job's setup page (Job → Setup/Settings)
scenarios.details: Successfully navigated to /jobs/15819/setup/details. The job setup page loaded correctly with sidebar links including 'Automations'.

scenarios.description: Find the 'Automations' or 'Apply Response Template' section
scenarios.details: Successfully navigated to /jobs/15819/setup/automations. The page shows 'Automations' heading with an 'Application confirmation' section containing 'Custom confirmation message' dropdown (currently 'Disabled').

scenarios.description: Verify a Subject input exists for the apply response template
scenarios.details: No Subject input field exists on the automations page. The 'Application confirmation' section contains only the 'Custom confirmation message' enable/disable dropdown. The accessibility snapshot confirms no textbox with 'Subject' label exists anywhere in the automations page DOM. Code inspection confirms: the current branch's JobSetupAutomations.tsx manages only useApplyResponseTemplate and applyResponseTemplate state — no applyResponseTemplateSubject. The messaging-improvements branch DOES add a FormInput for 'Subject' with name='applyResponseTemplateSubject' between the enable/disable dropdown and the ProseMirrorEditor body. This is a deployment/branch issue, not a code bug.
scenarios.expected: A text input labeled 'Subject' should appear in the Application confirmation section when custom confirmation is enabled
scenarios.actual: No Subject input exists. Only the Custom confirmation message dropdown and the message body editor are present.
scenarios.root_cause: Feature code not deployed to running server — wrong branch

scenarios.description: Verify subject is pre-populated with '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}'
scenarios.details: Cannot verify — Subject input does not exist on running server. Code review of messaging-improvements branch confirms the implementation sets default to '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}' via: passedJob.applyResponseTemplateSubject || '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}'.

scenarios.description: Change the subject to something custom, save — verify it persists on reload
scenarios.details: Cannot verify — Subject input does not exist on running server. Code review confirms the messaging-improvements branch sends applyResponseTemplateSubject in the updateJob mutation call.

code_review_notes.observation: Subject field implementation looks correct: FormInput with name='applyResponseTemplateSubject' is placed inside FormConditionalFields (shown only when useApplyResponseTemplate is enabled), between the enable dropdown and the ProseMirrorEditor body. Default value falls back to '{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}'. Subject is included in the updateJob mutation payload.

No apply_response_template_subject column on jobs table. The jobs table has apply_response_template (string) and use_apply_response_template (boolean) but no subject column. The migration from the feature branch has not been applied.

screenshots.description: Automations page showing Application confirmation section with only Custom confirmation message dropdown — no Subject input field

additional_observations: The automations page has an intermittent redirect issue: after loading, the app sometimes navigates away to the candidates inbox view (/jobs/15819/stages/110706/applicants/12137/...). This happened consistently during testing and may be related to a React Router redirect or notification polling. This is unrelated to the email-subjects feature but worth noting as it affects testability.

The single-send message composer (visible on the candidates messages tab) DOES show a Subject field pre-populated with 'Software Engineer at Acme Inc.' — but this was observed on the candidates page, not the automations page, and may or may not be from the feature branch.
